title: Greek Lemon Chicken & Potatoes
description: Bone-in skinless chicken thighs and potatoes roasted in a blended lemon, garlic, and oregano drizzle until the potatoes soak up all the pan juices and the chicken browns deeply.

ingredients.name: potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F fan). Add {8} extra virgin olive oil, the zest and juice of {9} lemons, {10} garlic cloves, {13} Dijon mustard, {12} honey, {11} stock, and a pinch of salt and pepper to a blender. Blend until smooth and emulsified.
Heat {3} olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium. Add {2} onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add {1} potatoes to the pan. Pour over roughly half the blended lemon drizzle, season with {4} oregano and a little of the {5} salt and {6} black pepper, and toss to coat.

Nestle {0} chicken thighs on top of the potatoes. Pat the chicken dry if needed — skinless thighs won't crisp the same way as skin-on, so dry surface is important. Season with remaining {5} salt and {6} black pepper.
Roast uncovered at 180°C fan for 60 minutes, until the chicken is deeply golden and cooked through (165°F internal) and the potatoes are tender and have absorbed the pan juices.
Remove from oven. Pour the remaining lemon drizzle over everything and finish with {7} fresh parsley. Serve straight from the pan.

notes: Skinless thighs won't get quite as lacquered as skin-on, but the browning is still good if they go in dry and uncovered the full hour. Use low-sodium stock to keep the salt in check — the miso pulls enough sodium from the other components. The blended drizzle is the soul of this dish; don't skip the blender step, whisking won't fully emulsify it. Leftovers reheat well — the potatoes actually improve overnight.
